fluff.overview: The Hunchback IIC was developed by Clan Smoke Jaguar around 2856 as a Clan-technology rebuild of the venerable Inner Sphere Hunchback. Deliberately underarmored and ammunition-starved, the design was originally intended as a punitive assignment for disgraced warriors, virtually guaranteeing a short and violent combat career. A celebrated engagement in 3015 rehabilitated the Hunchback IIC's reputation, transforming it from a symbol of shame into a weapon of fierce Clan pride. Since that turning point, the design has maintained a consistent presence of roughly three percent of every Clan's total touman, with production spread across multiple Clan worlds to sustain the high attrition rates inherent to its aggressive combat profile.
fluff.capabilities:
The Hunchback IIC centers its combat capability on a pair of Devastator Ultra AC/20s, among the most powerful weapons in the Clan arsenal. These twin autocannons can deliver catastrophic damage to any opponent at close range, but carry a combined total of only ten rounds between them, creating severe ammunition constraints that define the design's tactical profile. A pair of Series 7J extended-range medium lasers mounted in the center torso provide token supplementary firepower, though they are frequently overlooked in the chaos of close-range combat.

Six tons of Series Ab armor offer minimal protection for a fifty-ton BattleMech, leaving the Hunchback IIC critically vulnerable to sustained fire. The General Systems 200 XL engine provides a maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, while jump jets serve primarily to close distance for optimal autocannon engagement rather than provide true tactical mobility. The design is exceptionally lethal in its opening engagement but possesses virtually no endurance for prolonged operations, a characteristic entirely consistent with its original purpose as a weapon of last resort for condemned warriors.
fluff.history:
Clan Smoke Jaguar introduced the Hunchback IIC as a deliberate instrument of punishment, assigning the underarmored and ammunition-starved design to warriors marked for disgrace. Inner Sphere intelligence initially interpreted the machine as a last-chance glory weapon for aging warriors, missing the more calculated cruelty of its true purpose.

The design's reputation shifted dramatically following the Star of Rage incident in 3015 on Circe. Five outspoken Warden MechWarriors, reassigned to defend a Smoke Jaguar production facility and given Hunchback IICs as a clear signal of their diminished standing, faced a Jade Falcon Trial of Possession for their BattleMech Star. The five warriors responded with overwhelming aggression, decimating the Falcon force in under ten minutes. This victory transformed the Hunchback IIC from a symbol of shame into a weapon of fierce Clan pride.

In the wake of the Star of Rage, Clan Jade Falcon sibkin adopted the Hunchback IIC as a preferred platform for their initial Trial of Position, using its devastating firepower to secure quick kills. While veteran warriors derided this practice as lacking honor, it proved undeniably effective for blooding new fighters and rapidly expanding unit rosters. Despite staggering attrition rates, every Clan maintains Hunchback IICs at roughly three percent of their total touman, with production spanning multiple Clan worlds ensuring a constant supply of replacements.

Several variant configurations emerged over time to address the base model's severe limitations. Inner Sphere salvagers who acquire Hunchback IICs typically strip at least one Ultra autocannon to free tonnage for additional armor and supplementary weapons, fundamentally altering the design's Clan-intended purpose. By the Dark Age era, production had spread beyond traditional Clan facilities, with Red Devil Industries on Pandora contributing new variants under both Lyran Commonwealth and later Jade Falcon ownership.
fluff.deployment: The base Hunchback IIC configuration serves across virtually every Clan touman, though Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Jade Falcon have historically fielded the largest numbers. Jade Falcon sibkin in particular favor the standard configuration for initial Trials of Position, where its overwhelming short-range firepower can secure decisive kills before ammunition constraints become relevant. Despite staggering attrition rates inherent to the design's thin armor and limited endurance, steady production across multiple Clan worlds ensures replacement chassis remain available. Inner Sphere forces that acquire Hunchback IICs through salvage typically modify them extensively, stripping at least one autocannon to redistribute tonnage toward survivability.
